title: Shrink short attention window (seq_len//4)
description: Changed short_window from long_window//2 to long_window//4 in _compute_window_sizes (train.py), at WINDOW_PATTERN=SSSS, DEPTH=9 baseline; all other hyperparameters unchanged.
reflection: val_bpb 0.992950 vs 0.998440 baseline, a 0.0055 improvement -- the biggest single-run win since DEPTH=9 (0.0037) and clearly outside noise (prior nominally-identical reruns differ by ~0.00002-0.00005). Confirms the mechanism from the SSSS win generalizes: cutting attention compute per step (here via window size, not just frequency) buys more steps/tokens in the fixed 5-min budget and that outweighs the reduced context per step at this scale. Peak VRAM actually went up slightly (61.9GB vs presumably similar/lower for SSSS-half) likely just run-to-run noise in allocator behavior, not a real increase (window shrink should only reduce attention memory). Natural follow-up: bracket further, e.g. seq_len//8, to see if this is monotonic or has a sweet spot -- worth a confirming rerun before fully trusting given it's a single data point, same caution the group applied to the SSSS win before trusting it.
